sections.html:
Taxes are paid to the Tax Collector's office in the municipal building, 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723. It opens on weekdays at nine and closes at four. One bill folds in municipal government, public school, county government, library, open space and fire district taxes. Not receiving a bill does not excuse payment, and interest still runs.

Brick sits in Ocean County, so assessment disputes belong to the Ocean County Board of Taxation, reachable at 732-929-2008. Send every appeal question there, not to the collector.

Brick covers 32.22 square miles, a fifth of it water, and had an estimated 77,402 residents in 2025. Owners occupy 82.2 percent of households, and the middle value for an owned home is $410,600. Much of the housing came with a long boom that followed the opening of the Garden State Parkway in 1954, in neighborhoods such as Lake Riviera, Laurelton and Baywood.

The Parkway cuts through the west side with exits 89, 90 and 91, and routes 35, 70 and 88 cross town. NJ Transit buses reach Midtown Manhattan, Newark and Camden, and a Park and Ride at Exit 91 offers an express run to New York City at rush hour. Commuters are a large share of the buyer pool.

The year is billed in four quarters, and each falls due on the first of its month. A 10 day grace period follows, and interest attaches to anything received later.

A seller who is behind on any installment should get the balance, with interest, from the collector before a closing is scheduled.

Choose the method with the grace period in mind. Counter payments accept check, cash or credit card, and checks can be mailed to the same address. Online payment runs through Paymentus.

  • Cards online cost a 2.5 percent fee and post the next business day.
  • E-checks sit through a 10 business day hold under bank network rules, so they can land after the grace period and draw interest.
  • Automatic withdrawal needs a short form and a voided check, adds no cost, and pulls funds inside the grace period. Cancel in writing before a due date.
  • Never mail card numbers, and expect no Paymentus option for tax sale items or lien redemptions.

To redeem a lien, write at least 72 hours ahead with the block, lot and lien number and the date payment will reach the office. Certified funds, cash or a money order are the only forms accepted.

It is the extra tax on new construction. When work is finished, the township assesses the improvement and mails an Added Assessment Bill in October, payable November 1 with the fourth quarter, then February 1 and May 1 of the following year. It is combined with the regular bill that arrived in June or July, and the next June bill merges everything.

Unpermitted work tends to surface at sale. A buyer's inspector asks for proof that additions were approved, and state law lets officials levy up to $2,000 plus $2,000 for each week a violation continues. Sales have collapsed or dropped in price when such work was found. Pull your permits and final approvals for any finished basement, deck or addition before you list.

No certificate of occupancy is demanded when a Brick house is resold. The seller must still get the Bureau of Fire Safety's compliance certificate for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher, and the bureau's number is 732-458-4100. An oil tank in use and not leaking can stay put, and removal becomes a point for the buyer and seller to negotiate.

  • Rentals need a certificate for each new tenant, and landlords register through the Township Clerk for $100.
  • Weeds and grass may not top 10 inches.
  • Unregistered vehicles belong in a garage, not on the lot.
  • Owners clear the sidewalk and the strip to the curb, snow included.

For flood zones, check FEMA's lookup, but know that only a surveyor can settle one.

The Ocean County Board of Taxation decides assessment appeals. State rules put the petition date at April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation or reassessment. Build the case on recent sales of similar homes, and keep paying installments while it is pending.

Appeals matter to a seller mostly because a lower assessment can make the house easier to sell. Weigh the effort against your timeline, since a case filed in spring may not be decided before you close.

An unpaid installment does not block a sale. The collector's payoff, with interest, comes out of your proceeds at closing. Ask for it in writing, dated for the closing day, and hand a copy to the title company.

If a cash buyer is on the other end, the same steps apply. The difference is that nobody waits on a lender, so the payoff letter and your permits are usually the only items that set the pace.

sections.h2: Steps to take before you list a Brick house
sections.html:
Begin with the collector. Ask for a written payoff that shows every installment paid and any interest owed, and note whether an Added Assessment Bill is still running. Then pull permits for anything built after the house was first assessed, including a finished basement, a deck or an addition. Last, schedule the Bureau of Fire Safety inspection for smoke detectors, carbon monoxide detectors and a fire extinguisher, so the certificate is ready when a buyer asks.

If the house is a rental, add the tenant certificate and the registration record. Sellers who finish these items before listing tend to spend less time in negotiation, because the buyer's inspector has fewer surprises to raise.

Each quarter covers three months, and the bill is a single figure that already includes municipal government, school, county, library, open space and fire district taxes. When you sell, the contract usually divides the quarter in which you close between you and the buyer by the day. Your attorney will explain how it is done, and the settlement statement shows your share.

Because the grace period is only 10 days and e-checks can take 10 business days to clear, sellers who pay close to the deadline should use a method that posts quickly. A late installment adds interest to the payoff, and that number is what the title company will collect from your proceeds.

faqs.q: Where is a Brick property tax payment made?
faqs.a: At the Tax Collector, 401 Chambers Bridge Road, Brick, NJ 08723, in person between nine and four on weekdays, by mail, or online through Paymentus, which charges 2.5 percent on cards.

faqs.q: Which board decides a Brick assessment appeal?
faqs.a: The Ocean County Board of Taxation, at 732-929-2008. The petition date is April 1, or May 1 after a municipal revaluation or reassessment.

faqs.q: Is there any grace after a Brick due date?
faqs.a: Yes, 10 days. Interest applies after that, and e-checks may miss the window because of a 10 business day processing hold. Direct withdrawals from a bank account draw during the grace period.

faqs.q: Must a Brick seller obtain a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: No, the township does not ask for one on resale. A fire safety certificate is still needed, and the Bureau of Fire Safety at 732-458-4100 issues it.

faqs.q: What does Brick mean by an Added Assessment Bill?
faqs.a: It is the bill for finished new construction, mailed in October. It comes due November 1, then February 1 and May 1 the next year, and the following June bill merges it with the regular tax.
